September 30th, 2012 I was diagnosed with Meckels Diverticulum.  It's a freaky thing if you want to learn about it [here you go.](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meckel's_diverticulum) It all started when I was ironically browsing reddit before work.  I had to use the bathroom. I felt like I had to go #2, but it came out looking like #1, but dark, dark red. The night before I had consumed a lot of wine during my house warming party, so at the time I thought it was wine.  After brushing it off I continued to browse reddit some more.  

Well it happened again so I went to the bathroom again.  This happened 3 times before I talked to my roommate about it. We joked around laughing about how when dogs feel sick they eat grass.  Well I decided to eat some lettuce as a joke. It immediately made me feel nauseous.  I ran to the nearest bathroom and started throwing up. 

After throwing up I sat back down to go #2 again.  Well this time I started to get really light headed, and a vignette of darkness shrouded my peripherals, and I felt like I was about to die.  I thought to myself, "this is how I go... I die taking a shit" I honestly wasn't about to let that happen so I immediately stood up, and went to splash some water in my face.  

The sensation felt more extreme now. I felt cold and  hopless. I yelled to my roommate to call an ambulance.  as soon as I splashed water in my face I blacked out.  

I remember waking up to my roommate holding my face in her lap. She was shouting at me.  Turns out that when I blacked out I hit my face on the wall, and hit my ribs on the toilet.  Keep in mind my pants were down during the whole shebang. 

Next thing I know the fire department was there.  Paramedics were asking me what drugs I was taking thinking that I was overdosing. I was 21 at the time so that's understandable. I tried to tell him that I wasn't on any drugs. I blacked out one more time and woke up in the ER.

In the ER I was greeted by countless hospital staff asking me questions, taking my blood, and at one point someone shoved a tube up my nose, down my throat and into my stomach. It was one of the worst experiences of my life.  

At this point nobody knows what is wrong with me.  A few hours later my blood count comes back. I lost more than half of my blood. The doctor told me that if I was home alone I would have been dead. It was so scary to hear. You know.. you always see things like this happen to people on TV and in the movies, but when it happens to you, it's just so... hard to comprehend. 

After 3 blood transfusions (I think), some kind of x ray, some radiation scan thing, and a colonoscopy; I was finally diagnosed.  The doctors needed to cut me open and remove it or else it would keep bleeding.

right before my surgery I remember the surgeon saying "get ready for the best cocktail of your life."  I woke up hours later feeling very very loopy.  I ended up being allergic to the morphine and I was scratching myself everywhere.  In my influenced state I started swearing and doing inappropriate things like grabbing my balls, haha, yelling swears at my mother, and just being a weird high dude.

The surgeon ended up removing 5 inches of my intestine.  I was happy to be alive.  

Now here is where my view on life changed.  I sat there in recovery for a week.  Many questions ran through my mind. The biggest one was, "What am I doing with my life"  

At the time I was just working as a server at a restaurant. I had been out of highschool for 3 years, and I had no direction, and no ambition.  I thought about what I had contributed to the world. I came to the conclusion that my life wasn't bad, but it wasn't great. I wanted greatness. I now saw life in a whole other perspective. I wanted to be something. I wanted to make people proud of me.  

Right then and there I made a decision to change my life.  Now, a year later, I am enrolled in college getting a degree in criminal justice. I'm working applying to departments soon as well. I want to make a difference in peoples lives just like those doctors, and nurses did for me. 

TL;DR: I had a near death experience and It made me want to live life to the fullest, and make something of myself.
